state: PR candidate; not merged or released

findings.summary: The old transport Stop incremented _responseGeneration before interrupt, discarding every later submit onState callback. A valid nonterminal interrupt reconcile then reactivated _sending/_streaming after the scaffold had been cleared, but the real terminal was fenced out forever.
regressions: H1 nonterminal Stop retains callbacks through wind-down and the real terminal unlocks Send
H1 Stop failure keeps the live observer and unknown outcome until an authoritative terminal
H1 delayed callbacks and submit completion from the stopped turn cannot overwrite a newer admission
H1 Stop and send keeps its new draft and never submits while the original recovery turn is still winding down
H1 real terminal during a held Stop wins over its late running read-back without relocking the composer
H1 real v2 wire keeps one submit, routes Stop to turn.interrupt and waits through running reconcile for terminal
findings.limitations: Real coordinator/journal/WsClient and loopback wire are covered; no phone or live remote recovery-v2 gateway was used. No unknown outcome is promoted to a terminal and no old prompt is resubmitted.

findings.summary: Stop was visible after v2 submit admission, while session open, write-ahead persistence or submit ACK could still precede the first state callback. With _activeClientTurnId null, the old code selected legacy interruptPrompt and revoked the v2 callback generation.
regressions: M3 Stop before the first v2 callback waits for its identity and interrupts exactly that turn once
M3 definite rejection before the first callback releases a queued Stop without a legacy interrupt or resend
M3 terminal first callback needs no interrupt and queued Stop does not reopen or resend the turn
M3 disposed queued Stop cannot interrupt a late admitted turn or emit UI after the route has left
M3 real v2 wire keeps one submit, routes Stop to turn.interrupt and waits through running reconcile for terminal
findings.limitations: A permanently unresolved submit may keep Stop intent waiting rather than fabricating terminality. The queued wait is released on route disposal. Stock gateways without the negotiated recovery-v2 contract retain their existing legacy path.

findings.summary: The old transport finally cleared _stopResponseInFlight without notifying the widget tree. Successful interrupt/reconcile paths often masked this by scheduling another setState; a held Stop error after disabled controls had rendered had no such state callback, leaving Send visually disabled after the boolean cleared.
regressions: L5 failed Stop releases Send without a subsequent transport callback, text edit, or history refresh
L5 nonterminal recovery Stop releases the visible Stop and Send gates without requiring another transport callback
L5 joined REST cancellation rebuilds Send after its Stop flight releases, without unrelated text or history changes
findings.limitations: The observed regression is the Stop-error branch, not all successful Stop paths. Success-only probes pass on the baseline and are retained as controls.

findings.summary: The streaming branch examined only nonempty composer text before returning. Staged attachments alone therefore led an enabled Send action to silently do nothing.
regressions: L6 attachments-only Send during recovery work gives visible feedback and preserves the staged file without interrupting
findings.limitations: Active-turn guidance intentionally remains text-only. This fixes the silent no-op with actionable feedback, not with a new attachment-steering or interrupt-and-resend feature.

findings.summary: Confirmed stalled HTTP 200/503 body and provisional-stop stalls. Apply a 60-second inactivity timeout to raw body events before UTF-8 decoding. Keepalives/tool/status/reasoning/fragmented bytes renew it; it is not a total-turn limit. Existing terminal authority, cancel-and-join, ownership, exactly-one callback and no automatic POST resend are retained.

Confirmed false has_more plus a short pinned-root page returned root while a current lineage tip remained at offset 50. Removed that shortcut. Retain client zero-new/pin-bound exhaustion and every async authority fence; an untagged exact fallback now requires its terminal probe.

Confirmed silent truncation with reported totals 0/1/3 and six real rows in response fixtures. This validates the response-contract defect, not a claim that a static stock server always miscounts. Removed total-driven termination; retain pin-bound zero-new window proof, requested-limit OFFSET advancement, deduplication, progressive snapshots, profile/query filters, cancellation and fail-closed maxPages cap.

Confirmed an opaque ID containing slash, question mark, fragment, percent, spaces and Unicode escaped its path segment. Encode only the session ID using Uri.encodeComponent, preserving configured prefix and the exact paging query.

Confirmed reset removed metadata but retained all secure bundles. Collect individually decodable saved IDs plus the sealed native binding; preserve raw pre-reset bundles, verify physical metadata removal before credential deletion, verify each deletion, restore exact raw bundles and metadata on failure, sanitize provider errors, and retain shared-list ownership/native mutation leases through settlement. Collect known certificate references only after confirmed commit; do not introduce a certificate plugin prerequisite on certificate-free/corrupt-key recovery. Regress same-ID queued replacement, lost/lying metadata ACK, delete ACK loss, failed verification/rollback and replayable native END.

Reject false/throwing Space writes; retain shared confirmed snapshots behind a dirty-key fence when repair fails. Serialize wrappers and require a successful fresh physical baseline before later mutations. Real Move/create/rename callers show safe localised failure feedback and Retry; rejected state never becomes a later save baseline.
Synchronous closed-owner invalidation, listener/flight cleanup, exact-socket fences and reentrant/queued callback fencing; preserve live replacement and open-owner rollback.
